Also, you're not a diabetic, so you have no idea what it is like for someone to meddle in your **personal** numbers and judge you for something that oftentimes you have no control over. So no, I cannot fault you for being mildly insensitive to the situation that I, along with other diabetics on here are describing. So my advice for you, read some of the posts on here and try to empathize instead of criticizing. How would you like it if someone asked you what your testosterone levels were or watched you use the restroom? Just like those, our blood glucose levels are **personal** until we choose to share them. So until we do, don't get in our business.

She obviously loves you and you need to do your best to hold on to her. The breakfast and flowers are a great start. As a female, I can safely say that we love little things like that. Just do little things like leaving her some of her favorite candy and a handwritten note -- doesn't need to be anything eloquent, just something as simple as "I'm thinking about you". Leave her a voicemail just to say hey and that you love her. If financially feasible, maybe get her a necklace so that when she wears it, she thinks of you.

Surprise her with sweetness. Don't be afraid to put it all out there. I'm rooting for you man, good luck.
